clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old female presented with right eye redness, pain, blurred vision, and photopsia, along with systemic symptoms including nausea, headaches, left shoulder pain, and long-standing night sweats. Initial ophthalmic examination revealed non-necrotizing scleritis, anterior chamber cells, vitreous turbidity, vitreous snowballs, papillary edema, and peripheral retinal lesions. Fluoroangiography showed peripheral vasculitis and papillitis. Further workup included an IGRA test for tuberculosis, which was positive but with negative Quantiferon (E007). This led to a PET-CT scan for exclusion of extra-pulmonary tuberculosis, which revealed hypermetabolic left supra-clavicular and mediastinal bilateral lymph nodes (E011). A lymph node biopsy was performed, confirming nodular sclerosing Hodgkin’s lymphoma stage IIB (E012). The patient subsequently underwent 6 cycles of ABVD chemotherapy, showing adequate tolerability, stable BCVA, absence of pain, but persistence of intermittent temporal right eye photopsia (E013).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with ocular symptoms including right eye redness, pain, blurred vision, intermittent temporal photopsia, non-necrotizing scleritis, endothelial haze, 1+ cells in anterior chamber, vitreous turbidity, inferior vitreous condensations, vitreous snowballs, papillary edema, and peripheral white/yellowish lesions.
Patient presented with systemic symptoms including nausea, headaches, left shoulder pain, and long-standing night sweats.

Fluoroangiography (FA) and indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) showed early arterial filling of central choriocapillaris, peripheral vasculitis, a hot disc papillitis appearance and peripheral hypofluorescent spots.
IGRA testing for tuberculosis came back positive but with negative Quantiferon.
A PET-CT scan revealed hypermetabolic left supra-clavicular and mediastinal bilateral lymph nodes, performed for exclusion of extra-pulmonary tuberculosis.
A lymph node biopsy came back positive for nodular sclerosing Hodgkin’s lymphoma stage IIB.
The patient underwent 6 cycles of ABVD chemotherapy, with adequate tolerability, stable BCVA, absence of pain, but persistence of intermittent temporal right eye photopsia.
